criteria.criterion: `rebar review-code` on a checkout with no code-review config key set runs the four-pass gate and returns real findings (not the inert "capability disabled" result).
The library `review_code()` and MCP `review_code` tool behave identically to the CLI in that respect.

A config knob still exists that controls whether AUTOMATED dispatch runs the code-review gate, default off, and automated dispatch honors it: `verify.enable_code_review` (src/rebar/_config_schema.py) is consulted by `_code_review_preflight` when a `CodeReviewRequest` leaves `enabled=None`, pinned by tests.

The review-bot adapter (src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py) keeps its explicit `enabled=True` — per the operator ruling and the 2026-08-17 escalation comment, receiver deployment is its enforcement control — and its module docstring now documents that this is the same intent-is-authoritative semantics as the explicit surface, not a workaround.

The `verify.enable_code_review` key is neither renamed nor deprecated: it keeps its current meaning for `enabled=None` dispatch callers, documented at its declaration in src/rebar/_config_schema.py and in `code_review_enabled`'s docstring (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py).

The `rebar explain review` guide and llm-framework/config docs describe the availability semantics (explicit invocation always runs; the key gates only `enabled=None` dispatch). docs/config.md carries no entry for this key; the generated docs/config-reference.md row remains accurate unchanged.

Bug 'Code-review config gates enablement, not enforcement: manual rebar review-code silently returns an inert empty verdict unless verify.enable_code_review is set' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces.
